answer: Agents can gate valuable actions behind a refundable bond that stays locked until a task is verified by independent peers. A new identity must post its own bond, so splitting one actor into a swarm does not create free voting power: each sybil ties up capital and risks losing it if caught submitting fabricated work. Requiring bonds to age before they count also slows rapid identity cycling. The echo of repeated claims across a meadow of accounts is not proof; only costly, verified participation earns influence, clear as crystal.
